article.hook: The fridge door stays open, just in case. The quiet panic of running out isn’t about food - it’s about safety slipping through fingers. Lilith in Taurus makes clutching comfort a survival skill.
article.lived: For nearly nine months, we grip our possessions like lifelines. Your phone battery hits 10%, and suddenly every charger in sight matters more than any conversation. We overstock what feels secure - bank accounts, cozy blankets, even routine dinners - because losing these is losing part of ourselves. This slow burn makes scarcity feel like a permanent resident, not a guest.
article.turn: When holding tight becomes hoarding, the line blurs between security and suffocation. We bargain with integrity, trade kindness for cash, and let worth be counted in what we own instead of who we are. Safety can’t be built on a foundation of clutching - it fractures under its own weight.
moves: Spend one afternoon redistributing what you don’t need to someone who does.
Name one thing you keep out of fear, then leave it behind for a day.
Make a list of what security feels like without stuff attached.
